result.summary: The gas safety certificate (CP12) at 22 Alder Way runs out in 9 days (19 Oct 2026). Nothing is booked, and the landlord hasn't answered two emails. I've queued a phone call asking him to approve the check (approval 36, about £85), emailed the tenant with an update and gas-smell safety advice, and moved the ticket to landlord_approval. I've also escalated it to a person at high priority, because a legal certificate is close to running out with no booking. The tenant also says she has never been sent a gas certificate. I put a 2-day hold on the ticket and recorded the key facts.

judgement.why_this_decision: The diary alert (event 004) says the CP12 expires 19 Oct with no booking. The landlord didn't reply to the 22 Sep and 2 Oct emails (events 001, 002). The compliance rules say to escalate when a certificate expires within 14 days with no booking, or when a landlord hasn't answered a compliance request after a follow-up. Both apply. Before escalating I tried a different channel: a phone call to the landlord on the number on file. The tenant's claim that she has never had a certificate (event 003) suggests a possible earlier breach, which needs agency judgement. I followed lesson #28 (a stalled approval goes to a person for a direct chase). I didn't follow lessons #15/#23 (keep waiting) because this is a legal deadline, not a routine repair.

alternatives_considered.option: Book a Gas Safe engineer now without approval
alternatives_considered.why_not: There is no pre-approved spend limit or standing authority on record. This isn't an emergency either: no gas smell or fault was reported. Whether the agency can book statutory checks without approval depends on the management agreement, so a person should decide that.

alternatives_considered.option: Send a third email and wait
alternatives_considered.why_not: Two emails have already gone unanswered and only 9 days are left. Another email alone isn't enough.
The tenant asked a direct question and was waiting for an answer. A phone call to the landlord is a reasonable next step the system can take.

Find earlier CP12s and send copies to the tenant, or review a possible breach if none exist.
